items.title: Cowboys' home-field advantage questioned as opposing fans take over AT&T Stadium
items.summary: SBJ's roundup of Dallas columnists describes 49ers fans filling AT&T Stadium for Sunday's 46-40 Cowboys loss, with 'Let's go Niners' chants and Cowboys players booed in warmups. The Fort Worth Star-Telegram's Mac Engel called it awkward and embarrassing but very profitable, noting a sellout is a sellout and that the Cowboys will not block resale the way some teams do. Jerry Jones said the club had known for weeks how many tickets 49ers fans were buying. The Dallas Morning News' Tim Cowlishaw argued modern US fans are more loyal to individuals and more willing to shift between teams than the home-club fans of the past.
items.what_it_means: A full stadium and a home crowd are different things, and a team that sells to whoever buys can bank the revenue while losing the atmosphere that makes the ticket worth having.

items.title: Relo Metrics data shows WNBA delivered $608M in sponsor value
items.summary: A Relo Metrics report says the WNBA generated more than $608M in sponsor media value this season, with broadcast value up 62% to $545M, or 90% of the total. The Indiana Fever, the only team with every game on national TV, drove $205M, or 37% of broadcast value, and new partners NBC, NBC Sports and USA Network added $105M. Around 85 brands generated more than $1M each, and financial services and healthcare, worth $123M combined, still have no dominant brand.
items.what_it_means: Women's sport sponsor value is growing fast but sits with the most-televised teams, and some big categories are still open for a brand to own.

items.title: Sports media's next growth phase centers on live events, direct distribution and new IP
items.summary: Panelists at SBJ's Media Innovators event said the next phase of sports media will be driven by new distribution, original storytelling and monetising live experiences. Horizon Sports & Experiences' David Levy called owning and creating live IP the biggest opportunity, combining events with VIP experiences, tickets and sponsorship, and said building an audience and collecting fan data are critical. The Suns and Mercury said reach and ratings have doubled and even tripled since moving to free over-the-air broadcasts with Gray Media, and DAZN's Walker Jacobs said the era of 125 million households paying for regional sports networks is never coming back.
items.what_it_means: As the old pay-TV bundle fades, properties are trading fees for reach and looking to live experiences and direct fan relationships for the next revenue stream.

items.title: Heat ready for 'A Night in Vice City' with plenty of GTA VI promotions
items.summary: The Miami Heat are staging 'A Night in Vice City' at Kaseya Center as a lead-in to the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, after more than two years of work with Rockstar Games that started when the team saw its arena in the game's trailer. The night includes a Vice-themed court, jerseys with nods to GTA VI and Travis Scott's Cactus Jack brand, GTA-inspired cars outside the arena, in-game music, and concession stands renamed after fictional GTA fast-food chains. Brand and chief growth officer Jennifer Alvarez called it a crossover bringing gaming and sport together in a new way.
items.what_it_means: Sports teams can borrow the pull of a bigger entertainment moment to reach fans who arrive through gaming and culture rather than basketball.

items.title: PGA Tour's Rolapp dishes on creating more media value, diversifying revenue streams
items.summary: Speaking at SBJ's Dealmakers event, PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said the sports business comes down to the product: get the most competitive product and people reward you with time and attention, and the commercial side follows. He said US media rights are a $30B a year business that will keep rising as money moves from scripted programming to live sport, but warned it will not feed everything. Rolapp said the Tour's 47 events had been spread across the calendar in ways fans didn't understand, with diluted fields, and that the 2028 Championship series is designed to create scarcity and more media value.
items.what_it_means: Rising rights money will go to the properties that win fans' time, so scarcity and a clearer product matter more than more inventory.

items.title: NFL's Germany Matchup Makes Case for More Sunday Morning Games
items.summary: Fox drew an average US audience of 12.15 million for the Lions' win over the Patriots in Munich, the largest Sunday morning audience for any NFL game on any network. The game opened a Fox tripleheader that Fox says totalled 10.6 billion minutes of viewing, the most-watched regular-season Sunday on one network in NFL history. FOS says the result adds to the likelihood of Sunday morning becoming a permanent fourth window, which an 18-game season would help support.
items.what_it_means: International games are creating new broadcast inventory at home as well as new fans abroad, which raises the value of the league's schedule.

items.title: Why Geico bet big on a youth sports docuseries
items.summary: Geico's eight-episode docuseries Miles that Matter, now on DAZN, follows Greg Olsen, Luke Kuechly and Jonathan Stewart coaching a Charlotte middle school football team. Geico's VP of integrated marketing and media Kate Jalkut said live games show fans the athlete, and the brand wants to tell more stories about the person. Marketing Brew says the series is part of a storytelling-led era of Geico's sports marketing, aimed at connecting with fans beyond plays and highlights to compete for consideration in insurance, and designed not to be overly branded.
items.what_it_means: Sponsors are funding original sports storytelling to earn attention between games, using content as a way into consideration in a crowded category.

items.title: RBC City National Bank renews Golden Knights sponsorship for 10 years
items.summary: RBC City National Bank has renewed its founding Golden Knights sponsorship for 10 years, keeping naming rights to the practice facility through 2037 and expanding its rights across owner Bill Foley's portfolio, including the AHL Silver Knights, IFL Knight Hawks, Foley hotels, wineries and AFC Bournemouth. Terms were not disclosed, but business president John Penhollow called it the team's most lucrative corporate partnership and believes it is the NHL's most valuable practice-facility deal. The Golden Knights do not control naming rights to T-Mobile Arena, which makes the practice facility key inventory.
items.what_it_means: Owners with several properties can sell sponsors a whole portfolio of fans and venues, which can grow a deal beyond what one team could offer.

items.title: TikTok says 94% of songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 went viral on its platform first
items.summary: TikTok's 2026 Music Impact Report, prepared by Luminate, says 94% of songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 went viral on TikTok before charting, up from 84% in 2024. Songs that went viral spent an average of eight weeks on the chart against two weeks for those that didn't, and reached a median peak of No. 79 against No. 120. The virality and engagement data in the study was provided by TikTok.
items.what_it_means: Discovery for music now happens largely on one social platform before the charts, which shapes where artists and promoters build demand.

items.title: Alexis Ohanian: Women's sports growth 'still just beginning'
items.summary: Speaking on Bloomberg's The Deal, Reddit co-founder and team owner Alexis Ohanian said US women's sports are in the third or fourth inning and globally still in the first. He said brands are showing a lot of energy but women's sports media is fragmented, with no critical mass yet for a brand that wants to buy into the bigger media story. He said there is not enough inventory for all the brand demand in women's sports.
items.what_it_means: Brand demand for women's sport is running ahead of the media inventory available to buy, which favours whoever builds scale first.
